note: Source typo: <milestone unit="seciton" n="128"/> (misspelled "section") treated identically to a normal section milestone.

This witness carries no section divs at all; every section boundary above was reconstructed from inline markers, which frequently fall mid-paragraph. A handful of quoted-verse blocks (the "Marius" fragment, the Aratus/Prognostica translation) are printed as a bare ... sitting between two

elements rather than inside either; captured regardless since this importer reads all text within a Book, not just text inside a

.

Book 1 section 25 has no <milestone unit="section"/> of its own in this witness (a genuine gap, not a duplicate - contrast the companion De Senectute English witness's "35"/"35b" duplicate). Book 2's own section-milestone sequence is complete (1..150, no gaps). Nothing is fabricated; section 25 is present and complete in the Latin sibling (data/de-divinatione-la).

289 <note> translator's footnotes (Falconer's own cross-references and commentary, not the translated running text) were excluded entirely, tag and content; not logged individually given their routine, uniform nature.
5 <bibl> citation gloss(es) identifying the source of a quoted verse fragment (not Falconer's translated text) were excluded entirely, tag and content.

130 chapter milestones and 281 section milestones captured (1 of the latter spelled "seciton" in the source, treated identically); each section's Division.ref is the chapter citation active when that section's milestone fired. Passage.ref is always null.
